text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sweet Corn 16 oz #10 Can Big fan of prepping for emergencies and whatever else that may impact food supplies. I buy from Augason Farms regularly. I have never had any major issues or concerns with any of their products. Sellers yes, products no. I buy emergency food and tuck it away. I try to buy when on sale because I am basically buying food and not eating it. I rarely get into it, or rotate it. If I am buying from Augason farms, then the packaging is just fine for super long term storage (10-25 years depending on the food item). I get the occasional dented can (this one was fine), and it makes no impact. It isnt like other food grade cans where the can is breeched. These cans are made to withstand floods and other crazy stuff. They float, did you know that? Sometimes I will get into a can early if I bought it on sale and it is same price or cheaper than non long term storage equivalent (recently I experienced that with powdered butter. My usual bagged brand was more expensive than the sale price of Augason powdered butter.. stuff like that).

Anyway, I like the corn to be consumed as is, tossed in a big bowl of salad, or rehydrated when used in soups or as a side. Not my number one prep item, but it does add variety.

Occasionally I see people post reviews that say they got an expired product. But they never show a picture of the date they are looking at. The cans show the manufacture date first and foremost, then follows the best by date many many many years in the future. If they got an expired product, then do the math. That means the product would have been made 10-25 years ago. I mean, maybe. Lets see the label. They change the look of their label on occasion. So anyway, I am always suspect of those reviews. I just think they arent reading it right, and if it was legit they would post a pic of the can.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sweet Corn 16 oz #10 Can

Everything nests together perfectly—including the two plates, five bowls, bamboo stirrer and collapsible soup scoop, the pots with lids, and even a scrubber sponge!—and fits snugly in the included carrying bag. When I first pulled everything out, I tried the largest lid on the frying pan and it wasn't a tight fit. At first I thought that was a bad thing until I realized this is not a bulky set of kitchen pots and pans; the frying pan is just slightly larger than the largest pot so that the pot will nest into the frying pan to keep it all tidy and compact. The large lid, however, does cover the frying pan well enough to keep it from spattering.

At this price point, you couldn't ask for better materials. The only improvement that would be valuable to me is if the handles were coated with durable silicone instead of the red plastic. The plates are better quality melamine than the bowls, which are a thinner plastic, but they need to be thinner to fit so many into the kit.

The weight is a little less than 45 ounces, so it's not super lightweight, but for what's packed into this kit and the quality and versatility of the materials, I don't see how they could get it to weigh any less. We don't go camping much anymore, but what we will use this for is to keep at the ready along with an alcohol stove in case we have to be evacuated and wind up living out of our truck for a while! The kit will also be good to have on those few occasions when we have to cook for more than two people and need the extra pots and pans but don't have any place to store them in our small apartment. Because the handles fold against the sides of the pots, we could stick them into the fridge if there are leftovers until we can process or eat them.

text_fidelity_a: Gifts for Men Dad, Fathers Day, Husband Grandpa -Survival Kit Gear 16 in 1-Fishing Camping Hunting Hiking Gifts Ideas for Him-Cool Gadget Survival Gear We have been working on assembling a couple go bags for our family in case of an emergency, such as a natural disaster, fire, etc. WORSPODAY's 16-in-1 survival kit is the perfect addition to it. First of all, the price is on point and provides a huge savings over having to buy each of the items included individually. Second, we love the watertight hardback case that the tools come in. It has strong clasps on three sides and they don't just pop open. You have to tug pretty hard on them, so that actually is important so you don't lose your gear when you're on the move and may need it most. Second, the tactical gear that is included isn't cheaply made. These are durable products, such as the tactical pen (with a glass breaker on one end), flashlight (needs one AA battery), and the knife. Even the compass is fairly weighty in your hand and works very well. Also, because of the amount of detail that goes into these items, this whole kit makes a handsome gift that any outdoorsman would appreciate too. We also like the tactical bracelet because even if that is all you have on you, there is also a flint built in so you can start a fire, a whistle, and a compass. Also, it is made of paracord, so you can use it to tie up an emergency shelter or go fishing if need be. The manual that comes with it is detailed, but you will want to become well familiar with each item included and how to use it before you head out to the woods or on your trek as you may try to outrun a storm. Also, there are a few items included such as the glass breaker end of the pen, the saw, and of course the knife, which could cut someone, particularly a child, so you'll want to make sure those who handle it aren't going to accidentally injure themselves because these items are definitely not toys. All in all, however, this is an exceptional product, and I plan to recommend it to everyone I know who may be putting together their own go bag.

text_fidelity_a:
Myklops Rear View Mirror On the whole, I'm happy with my purchase and find it very useful when I'm riding. I've got a folding bike, which I love but limits my choice of mirrors. I tried different ones that attach to glasses or helmets, but I could never find one that quite fit; besides, I always worried they would drop off the moment I hit a bump. I figured the Myklops was my best option.

As others have noted, objects in this review are a heck of a lot closer than they appear. However, I've gotten used to this and find the mirror very helpful for spotting cars, trucks, and other larger vehicles in traffic. For spotting other bikes, skateboarders, and standing scooter riders (scooterists?), it's not as helpful. Being smaller, they're usually on me well before I pick them up in the mirror. Luckily, that's usually not a problem. With motorcycles and mopeds/scooters, it's a mixed bag. The bigger they are, they easier they are to pick out in the mirror. Usually it's the noise of their engines that I notice first, then I know to look for them in the mirror. So this mirror is helpful, but not as much as I'd like.

Sturdiness is hard to speak to without lots of time going by, but I've been using this regularly for over six weeks, tossing it into bags when I'm not riding with it, and it's holding up. I find the cover a little fiddly to close, but it does latch into place with a little patience. The biggest challenge was remembering to push the arms back into the base before taking by backpack off once I'd gotten to where I was going, but that's pilot error on my part. I don't yank at the arms or twist them hard, but neither am I super delicate with them. They feel the same as they did out of the package, so I'm hopeful that they'll last a while.

As for stability, I find the mirror to be very stable once I've extended the arms and positioned it how I like. The band sometimes shifts around my wrist as I ride, but I don't think this is a fault of the product. I usually wear long-sleeved shirts, the material of which is often a bit loose, so I need to be more careful about smoothing that down and not letting it bunch before fastening the strap. When I'm wearing shorter sleeves with tighter fitting sun gloves, the band stays in place. Also, I'm very pleased that the velcro on the band is on the gentle side. By that I mean that it doesn't have large teeth of the sort that often damage my clothes. Despite being careful, I sometimes catch my clothing on it, but so far (touch wood) it hasn't caused any pilling or tearing of the fabric ... and these are fairly delicate materials I'm talking about, so that's a major bonus.

I think it's impossible to make a perfect mirror that fits all my riding needs. But this comes pretty darn close. Funnily enough, as I sat down to write this review, I noticed that there's currently a nice little discount for it, no doubt for Black Friday/Cyber Monday/or other seasonal sales holiday here. I paid full price for mine, but I'm okay with that. At full price, I feel like I got my money's worth, and I would definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: Myklops Rear View Mirror

This lid is a great alternative if you want a simple one-handed open close that's still strong enough that it won't open by accident.

-easy one handed open
-if you look closely at the pictures there is a textured rubber grip that makes grabbing it from the top a more secure feeling
-the moveable handle is nice

Cons:
Like most of these snap lids, the trade-off is slightly less insulation then the HydroFlask brand lids. When I did a side-by side test with several of my Hydro Flask lids, this Takeya melted ice faster than the hydroflask. This is still not too bad as the water was still cold, just not quite as cold as a stock hydroflask lid

Who this is for: You want a more convenient drinking experience and hate the Hydro Flask brand options. Good for one-handed open/close

Who this isn't for: If you must have long-lasting ice in your container for as much time as possible.

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Personal Safety Kit With Pepper Spray and Personal Alarm, 25 Bursts, Intuitive Finger Grip, 120dB Alarm, Audible Up To 1,280-Feet (390-Meters) I have never used any type of pepper spray or personal safety items. I thought it might give some peace of mind during some situations. The items are two separate devices, so there are two things to keep track of. Ideally, it would be great if they were combined somehow into one device. Both items have a key chain attachment so you can keep it with your keys. I have put them on a lanyard instead though, for fear of accidently setting them off. I keep the lanyard inside the outer pocket of my purse. I can also wear the lanyard around my neck if desired. I was afraid to test these items, but I did. To activate the alarm, you pull the pin with the key chain. Once it's removed, a loud, piercing sound is made. It frightened the cats immediately! It wasn't too loud that it hurts your ears. It kind of reminded me of a car alarm sound. The alarm stops when you reinsert the pin and click it in place.  My husband and I tested the pepper spray outside. It was a windy day, so we made sure that we didn't spray it against the wind. A reddish orange stream of pepper spray was dispensed. The description of the product says it goes about 10 feet. We didn't measure it, but that seems pretty close to what we got. I like that you get about 25 sprays from it. I did get some on my finger. It dripped down from the dispenser. I immediately wiped my hand on the grass, then went inside and washed it thoroughly.  I was able to get it off because it didn't burn or sting. It doesn't have much of a smell. Hopefully, I won't have to use these! There is an expiration date on the pepper spray which is good to know.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Personal Safety Kit With Pepper Spray and Personal Alarm, 25 Bursts, Intuitive Finger Grip, 120dB Alarm, Audible Up To 1,280-Feet (390-Meters)

text_fidelity_a:
Black Mountain Products Resistance Band Set with Door Anchor, Ankle Strap, Exercise Chart, and Carrying Case I bought this set of bands to work on rehabbing my knee outside of the gym. This type of product is certainly convenient to use and offers a fair amount of resistance for my purposes. However, for those intent on building gobs of muscle, weights are of course ideal. I found that I needed some time to adjust to the feel of these bands. While the manual indicates some type of pound rating it doesn't feel accurate. The nominal rating of weak to strong is a better way to judge the resistance of each band. I chose a familiar exercise that would allow me to work through a range of bands. I knew what I could lift with weights and compared that sensation to the band with a similar resistance. From there I could start to estimate which bands i might start with for other exercises. The kit is nicely put together with a wide range of bands and extra straps for doors and ankles. The carrying bag holds everything without being cramped and is well suited for travelling. As another reviewer noted, the bands are rubber and are subject to wear. It behooves the user to inspect them regularly before use.

Update: I have used this kit several times now and wanted to add a finding. I found the exercises more satisfying when contracting and holding the muscles being worked on at the end of the positive movement. This gives extra focus to the area at hand and makes the most out of the resistance that the bands offer. Hopefully, I am not overstating the obvious, but I found this feature easier to do with the bands than with free weights.
text_fidelity_b: Black Mountain Products Resistance Band Set with Door Anchor, Ankle Strap, Exercise Chart, and Carrying Case

Yoga Mat - With Carry Strap -Great Pilates And Exercise Mat With Carry Sling -Save on Yoga Mat Bag-Best Classic Yoga Mat - 1/8" (3mm) Thick -Great Workout Mats For Women Kids And Men- Eco Friendly- Best Non-Slip Yoga Mat for Carpet, Home And Travel-On Sale-100% Money Back GUARANTEED! (Purple) NOTE: I received a free sample of this yoga mat for review purposes.

I have been practicing yoga for almost 15 years, and during that time, I have owned approximately ten different mats. My favorite is the one that I currently use both at home and for my classes, which is my [[ASIN:B00AB3LLVS Manduka eKO Lite Yoga Mat]]--I prefer its relatively thin profile, and it is one of the few mats that I have tried that is completely non-slip. However, my very first mat--an inexpensive version purchased at a discount clothing store--has a nice pebbled texture that has continued to perform quite well. (I keep that one at work.)

Yet, I'm always interested in trying new mats, as I donate them to others if I can't use them myself. This mat is an attractive purple color, and it comes with a convenient slip-on carry strap, something that most of my other mats don't have (I generally use a mat bag for class). What is most remarkable about this mat, however, is that is absolutely the LIGHTEST mat I have ever owned/used--to the point of feeling quite flimsy. Although it is the exactly same width as my Manduka Lite (3mm), the material of this mat has absolutely no substance to it, lacking the weightiness of my Manduka mat. Still, a lightweight mat is not necessarily a bad thing, as it can be convenient for travel. And one nice thing about this mat is that it is actually thin enough that it can be folded (again, it is thinner than a Gaiam mat I have which is DESIGNED to be folded), so that could come in handy for those wanting to stash a mat in their suitcase.

With respect to performance, however, I found this mat to be disappointing. Although this mat felt fairly secure for standing postures, no matter what I tried, my hands slipped on the mat in downward facing dog. I certainly would NOT feel secure attempting arm balances on this mat! Furthermore, although the mat is described as "eco-friendly," the only evidence of this appears to be that it uses "Phthalate-free inks"--no other information is provided about whether the mat's materials are from natural sources, such as rubber or bamboo.

In the end, I would recommend this mat ONLY if you are looking for a yoga mat that is super-lightweight and can fold into a suitcase. Otherwise, there are better choices available, and you can likely find better options at your local big box store.

text_fidelity_a: KME Precision Knife Sharpening System The main reason I bought this sharpening system over edge pro, wicked edge or tsprof was the fact that it has a handle and I can use it while sitting in my chair watching TV. I know myself and I am waaay more likely to use something like this more often if I can use it while sitting in my chair so this review is based on using it that way. It came with a letter from the company providing ways to contact them directly if there is any issue which is awesome, and the instruction manual was very clear and easy to understand with good pictures. I've always been scared to ruin my factory edges since I have never been able to get them as sharp again so I have been only stropping which works great until you get real damage which I did a few weeks ago when I dropped my ferrum forge gent on the concrete floor at work and chipped the edge. Given it was my first time using this sharpener I'd say it took about 30 minutes to get setup and work the chips out of the edge and go up to 1500 grit. It was a great edge at that point, but you should definitely get the strop that fits in there. It is very sharp at 1500, but the edge isn't really polished at that point. After using the strop that fits in there it not only looks great, but it is an edge that I have never seen from any of my knives before. It is truly scary sharp. Like not popping hair sharp, but no pressure at all and the hairs just go away without even noticing that it happened sharp. I will be redoing the factory edge on all my knives over the next few weeks. The only con I noticed is that it is a bit awkward when changing between stones. You have to be very careful of the knife edge while putting force on the knob that holds the stones in. Speaking of which, you have to get the knob on the stones quite tight for it to stay in place well. Other than those 2 things, which are quite minor (and the first one is almost certainly only due to me doing this in my recliner haha) this thing is freakin amazing. Highly recommended!
text_fidelity_b: KME Precision Knife Sharpening System

I have very little fat or muscle on my fingers, and so when a frisbee knocks my hand the wrong way, I get huge purple bruises and welts on my hands and wrists which make playing frisbee with a traditional frisbee not very fun.

The Superdisc, by contract, has a soft rim of that Aerobie rubberized plastic which makes it easier to catch without hurting delicate hands. It flies forever, and the weight balance feels perfect. I played this indoors, in a tiny park, and at the beach over distances so large that we couldn't even shout at one another. It worked great and was a blast in every setting.

Only thing I wish is that we could choose our colors. I'd like the girly hot pink, while my partner hoped for a blue. We got a yellow one. You get what you get, apparently.

Overall this is well worth the price, and even if you throw it in the ocean as we did with our last Aerobie, it's still well worth it if you get at least a few games with it. We won't be without one now.
text_fidelity_b: Aerobie Superdisc Ultra, Colors May Vary

Sticky Holsters MD-1 - Suitable for Small 9MM’s - Med/Sm Autos up to 3.5" BBL Living in hot and humid Southwest Florida means that you get pretty darn hot and sweaty twelve months of the year. Since concealed carry became legal in Florida, I've been depending on a North American Arms .22 magnum stainless steel mini revolver for personal defense. Wearing shorts and any kind of shirt allows you to simply pocket the gun without any "printing" issues. No one knows that you have it, which is the way it should be. Until now I've been reasonably happy carrying this five shot .22 magnum loaded with high velocity CCI segmented ammo. It is impervious to sweat, is very light weight, and if anything ever goes wrong with it NAA will fix it for you--for free.

Now however our world seems a little more complicated. While most defense situations take place within three yards, my little .22 magnum is going to leave me out-gunned in capacity, stopping power, and potential range. With those thoughts in mind, I purchased a Springfield Armory XD Mod-2 Subcompact in .45 acp. It has everything that I was looking for but is considerably heavier. Rather than jump from one extreme to the other, I decided to buy a Sticky Holster for my Kahr CM9 (9mm) and work with that first to adjust to IWB carry with a heavier and bulkier pistol. I'm a big guy, so wearing a light fishing shirt untucked with cargo shorts is a common sight here. While I am able to carry my Kahr in my right front pocket without printing issues, it is a little more difficult to draw it smoothly and consistently. And since pocket carry won't work for my new SA .45, I have been experimenting with placement inside my waistband.

I've been using the Sticky Holster now for over a week and no one has noticed that I'm carrying it--not even my wife. It works exactly as it's supposed to and I have not yet had the holster come out when I've pulled the Kahr. So I've found this holster to work as advertised and I've learned to become comfortable with the extra weight and size. Using this holster has also allowed me to learn where to place my new Stealthgear Onyx IWB when I decide to step up to the SA .45 Subcompact. My thoughts were that I would ditch the Sticky Holster when the Stealthgear comes in, but it is such a good fit for me that I'll probably also use it in the future. It's nice when something works as advertised.
text_fidelity_b: Sticky Holsters MD-1 - Suitable for Small 9MM’s - Med/Sm Autos up to 3.5" BBL

text_fidelity_a:
23-in-1 Survival Military Digital Watch, Mens Tactical Multi-Functional and Adjustable Wristband Outdoors Waterproof Sports Dual Dial Watches with Compass Paracord Band I got this watch originally to have on hand for any of us to use, but it turns out that my son is the only one that it fits.

DOES IT REALLY COME WITH ALL OF THESE THINGS?
Everything that is advertised that this watch has capacity to do it does. It has all of the bells and whistles on it, even the whistle which surprisingly came in handy the other night to chase an animal away when walking in the dark in our rural area.

WRISTBAND
The wristband of this watch is VERY bulky. I could not find a way to adjust it, so I could wear it, but our son fits in it perfectly. The paracord makes it bulky, but that is why it is a survival watch. It is not for looks, it is for practicality.

PERFORMANCE
The performance of this watch so far has served our son well. He can start a fire with it, even was able to tighten a screw. It was handy to have. It stays on pretty well with the clips and it is not too hard to use when you need to use one of the tools on board. So far, our son says that he likes it a lot and it performs well.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice watch with a lot of tools included with it. They have performed well so far, but the size is so big that only our son who has very bulky wrists can wear it.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I say four because it would be nice to be able to adjust the length. As for performance, it is doing well so far, so that is a big plus. The watch also works to this point also.
text_fidelity_b: 23-in-1 Survival Military Digital Watch, Mens Tactical Multi-Functional and Adjustable Wristband Outdoors Waterproof Sports Dual Dial Watches with Compass Paracord Band

I guess I should have watched some how to video's before hand because the instructions that came on the box were not sufficient enough.
Needless to say, I think I wrapped them wrong. I used the tape at the ends not at the beginning and I couldn't figure out how to get the plugs to stay in the handle bars. Since the bike I did didn't have the C shaped handles I only used slightly less than half of the tape.
I wish the kit would have came with more finishing tape since I did it wrong, but I’m still not sure if maybe I started at the wrong end.

Our 11 yr old son had got the hang of this, but broke his wrist in two places after it kicked out from underneath him when a wheel didn't cast over our smooth driveway as expected. Two surgeries, pins, screws, a titanium plate and a horrible permanent scar later, he now has use of his arm/wrist back until his 3rd surgery to remove the hardware this summer. Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency Purchased this Lighting Ever 1000 lumens lantern and the Rayovac Sportsman 240 Lumen LED Lantern SE3DLNACOM on the same order. Not realizing the identical nature of each lantern at the time, having both in hand together allowed me to make a side by side comparison. This might help someone chose which one to buy.

The Rayovac I purchased on this page shows a 240 lumen lantern, however the one that arrived clearly states 305 lumens. Physically, the LE and RV are manufactured almost identically in composition. Both require 3 D sized batteries to operate. The LE is only one ounce more than the RV, but the LE feels and looks sturdier and of higher quality. LE and RV will be used when describing each lantern, but keep in mind that I am comparing the Rayovac 305 lumen that arrived, versus what is advertised on the Amazon page.

The LE's output on highest mode is 1000 lumens compared to the RV's highest mode at 305; both are daylight white on high. On high, the LE touts a run time of 18 hours (10 watts), to the RV's 70 hours (4 watts), RV wins on run time.

The LE's second mode both reduces the lumens (dimmer) and changes the color temp to a warm white. While the RV does not have a color temp variable, it does provide an option to dim the output to 140 lumens for its 2nd mode and can run 140 hours. LE wins due to the option to change to preferred temperature color.

The LE's 18 hour operation will increase to 25 hours when on mode 2 (warm white). The third mode of the LE further dims the light and combines the warm and daylight temperatures to somewhere in between. The paperwork for the LE shows that mode 3 will last only 12 hours, which does not make sense as to why it shortens the life by the most .

The last mode for both (LE's 4th mode, RVs 3rd mode) is a blinking / strobe light of the daylight / cool white color. I've not much to say on this mode - does not seem relevant at the moment to me. The RV has one final feature though, which is a dim green light on the power button that blinks very slowly, to assist the owner in locating it during periods of darkness. Personally, I do not like this feature and would either remove the batteries or put a dimmit over the light. Buyers might prefer this, I'm just not a fan of idiot lights with or without power.

Lastly, I mentioned these being cut from the same mold, and both have battery compartments in the base of the lantern. The LE has a stem mounted in the base that the cover's slot must align correctly to close the battery compartment. The RV has a slot (no stem) on the rim of base to align to the cover's slot opening. However, the LE cover is still much easier to close with the batteries in the unit. Once the appropriate alignment is met, you must push down and turn to close the base. Think of pushing a child-proof pill bottle's lid to open it. Do the same on these lanterns. The LE base closed after 3 tries, to the RV's numerous tries getting frustrated. LE wins on battery replacement procedures.

Overall, the LE wins hands down. For a 15 ounce lantern with more features, I paid approximately 17.00. The 14 ounce RV cost $24, but the Amazon page shows the list price at $34 and the buyer was getting a $10 discount at purchase. Though the 4 watt RV runs much longer at 2.9 days or 5.8 on mode 2 and the 10 watt LE has a run time of .75 days or 1 full day on mode 2, I am not using this to go camping. This was purchased for power failures, to be used as part of an overall emergency preparedness plan, and bright is what we need indoors during power failures. The hours will be broken up over various times and 18 hours will get us several days. For the money, same battery requirements and functionality, LE takes the cake.

I've never heard of Lighting Ever before, but the product packaging shows they have their home base in Las Vegas, NV, another in the UK and one in China, where this lamp was made. It comes with RoHS certification, 1 year warranty and the instructions are the most accurate regarding the English language than I've seen in a long time. How refreshing to receive grammatically correct documents included in the box (yes, a real box). The RayOVac has a limited lifetime warranty and came in a plastic transparent bag, unbranded. The TLC shows on the LE, while the product packing on the RV is a wrapped label with specs, and it is though product presentation was an afterthought. For the $24, some type of protection during delivery wouldn't hurt. Whoever LE is, I will buy again if they produce a product as good as this one.
text_fidelity_b: Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency

text_fidelity_a:
ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large We have company coming this summer. This involves a few tents, but one of the people needs an inflatable mattress and room for stuff. This tent is who we got this for.

ASSEMBLY
Assembly was not difficult in our trial run. The instructions were pretty easy to follow and it does not take more than a half hour to put up with two people unless you are with someone VERY efficient in putting up tents.

WITHOUT FLY
Without the fly, this is a very nice tent - bright, airy, and lots of upper mesh to see the sky. This is perfect on nice days.

WITH FLY
The days that rain might be expected are the challenge. The fly is dark blue. The dark blue makes this tent feel very warm and almost oppressive some days, but it does protect in the rain. My point is if you are the type who does not want to take the fly off and put it on constantly, this might be a big dark for you to leave on constantly, unless you plan to just sleep inside and don't care.

STAKES
The stakes that come with this are not big enough to support the weight of wind and other frustrations. We got spiral stakes to use with this at least on the key points of stress and it works better.

STURDY?
We are only using this for this summer, so hopefully it will last through several weeks of use. We have not had any high winds or severe storms yet so I will have to update as to how well this worked for that.

STORM PROOFING
One thing we learned about tents over long term is that double tarps are a good idea. We put one down under the tent leaving a perimeter that is not too big around the edge. Then we put another inside the tent to further protect should there be a deluge.

STORAGE
I find that having a separate nylon bag for the fly helps a lot when it comes time to put this tent away. It allows for a faster pick up time and less frustrating trying to make everything fit.

SIZE
This is perfect for a queen sized mattress, 1 or 2 people and their stuff.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is great for a family with sleeping bags and not much stuff, or for less people and more stuff. The stakes could be better, the storage bag bigger, and perhaps a bit tougher construction/fabric, but all in all this is a decent tent and serves our purpose well- I hope.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS at this point. I will update once summer is over as to the longevity of this tent over several weeks.
text_fidelity_b: ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M I bought this from Amazon based on all the 5 star reviews. I have been wearing it consistently for 11 days and following the instructions as noted in the on-line user guide videos. I am torn as to whether to give this 3 or 4 start. I ended up going with 4 stars because I have tried other trackers and the REIGN feature-set is hands above the other devices I have tried. For me it is the best choice available, today.

PROS
SIZING: Band design and fit is excellent. You are given 3 band lengths with every device, which ensure you will get the perfect custom fit. Before you buy, I strongly recommend you go the the Jaybird REIGN site's FAQ pg for exact sizing info. http://www.jaybirdsport.com/static/img/reign/sizing-guide.jpg
Be aware, you want to determine the side-to-side width across the TOP of your wrist, not the circumference of your wrist. The REIGN is a 2 piece band. The fit/width of the top piece is what determines which size to buy. You then customize your fit with the bottom band, which is provided in 3 lengths.

SECURE: the magnetic locking mechanism ensures your band will never fall off. The design allows you to easily secure your band with one hand. Once it is magnetically secured, it will not come off until you manually disengage the magnets. Excellent design!

COMFORT: Due to the lightweight, smooth silicone band, this is the MOST comfortable activity wearable I have ever tried. As a tech professional, I am typing on my keyboard all day long and cannot wear any watch-type devices or jewelry on my wrists. This is the 1st tracker device I have found that I can wear all day, every day. I barely notice it's on my wrist. I wipe mine down with a damp cloth. I have had no irritation or discomfort. 5 stars!

TRACKING: The REIGN will track data by specific activity, which you will not get with other devices. It detects Walking, Swimming, Biking, Running and General activity. In addition to the 3 silicone magnetic wrist bands, they provide 2 stretch style athletic bands and an ankle biking band. The STEP tracking is accurate for me ( Compared my data for a couple of days with a FitBit and Treadmill)

SMART PHONE APP: The design of the SmartPhone app is a plus. The information provided is very good. In additional to your GoZone score, you are given 3 screens of data: Activity, Sleep and History. Each screen presents you with a Summary view and a Detail 'Timeline' view of that data.

VISUAL FEEDBACK: The band itself provides visual indication of your progress towards your GoZone Goal via lights. Each light represents 9% of your goal. (Dont bother enabling the 'Time' feature. The lights flash for 1 second and is pretty much useless)

CHARGING: Very easy to pop the device out of the band and charge on the charger that is included. Via USB cord, it can be charged thru your laptop or a plug, your choice. As stated, it takes about 3 hrs to initially charge. I pop mine onto the charger before I hop in the shower. Easy-peasy. Please note, if you lose the charger, you will have to buy a replacement since the charging doc is required.

USER GUIDE: I recommend you watch the online User Guide videos AND read thru the entire list of FAQs prior to purchasing/using the REIGN. There is a lot of info in the FAQs that is not covered in the User Guide videos that you will want to be aware of. A nice feature is, the videos are also part of the SmartPhone app.

HISTORY: the SmartPhone app. provides a History screen with Day, Week, Month & Year mode. Once you select your mode, you can then swipe thru by Day, Week, Month...... Very nice.

PERSONALIZED: The REIGN definitely does 'get to know you'. After the 1st week or so, the daily goal has adjusted, based on my history.

CONS:
GO ZONE: Upon waking up, you should be able to sync and log that day's GO ZONE feedback in 2 minutes. I have owned the REIGN for 11 days and rarely have I been ale to get GO ZONE to completed on the 1st try. Once the REIGN device is Connected to the SmartPhone app. and I Start Go Zone, I often get error messages and have to Start again. These issues are definitely specific to the GO ZONE feature, as I do not get errors throughout the day when syncing. This is the key feature of the device, so I expect it to work without issue and not have to battle with it.

SUPPORT: Unfortunately, I cannot give a good review on support. I sent a very detailed Email with screenshots from my SmartPhone listing the GoZone errors and Sleep monitoring issue I have experienced. The response I received was very friendly, however the only thing the reply told me was I could manually enter Sleep info in the app. There was no response to my detailed GoZone issues and questions.
SUPPORT Review Update 12-29-2015: I received another reply from Jaybird Support addressing my specific concerns and questions. They have provided me with instructions of how to reset my Reign pod, indicating this may resolve my specific issues.

READABILITY: I think the design of the app is great and it is easy to use. However, it is not so easy to read on your Smart Phone due to the funky color of the font (pale yellow-green) against a light grey background. It is not configurable. I understand these are the branded colors, but they do not lend themselves to readability on mobile devices.

DASHBOARD: There is not an online Dashboard. Your data is only available via your SmartPhone app. I went to the website and attempted to login assuming there would be an online dashboard. The online login is a separate account and is for purchases, only. The other tracker devices I have used have online Dashboards and settings, which I deem as a plus.

DATA SYNC: Data sync is on-demand, which preserves you SmartPhone battery (Yay!). However, for some reason, data for previous day(s) is not always shown in the app. Periodically, when you open the app on your phone, it will show all zero's after syncing. I have not been able to detect a pattern. It is an intermittent issue that cannot be reproduced, on demand. The work-a-round is to close and reopen the app.

TACTILE: Tapping the REIGN device 4 times does not active my lights. I have to rap it pretty hard, 8 to 12 times. I have mine set for progress feedback, only. The lights flash for 1 second. I would prefer a button that will allow me to quickly turn on the progress lights and turn them off when I release the button. ( If there were a manual button, the 'Time' feature may be of value).
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M

Coghlans 0008 Camp Knife This is just the right size for my medium size hands and disappears in my pocket. Fit and finish are great. There are no flaws in the Opinel blade locking ring, or handle. When properly locked open there is no play in the blade in any direction. Opening and closing the unlocked blade require a little effort which is the way that I like it. The wood handle is varnished. The locking ring is stiff and requires quite a bit more than my 12 year old Opinel. This is reported to ease up after using it for a while and I don't find it to be objectionable. Shaving sharpness is there too. This knife totally meets my expectations and requirements.
The dimensions of this knife are:

4-1/4" closed
3-1/4" Blade
7-1/2 Total Length open

The best attributes of this knife are the curved handle and the carbon blade. The standard Opinel handle is one of only two ways to get an Opinel with a carbon steel blade. It has a straight body with a larger bump on the end. The handle of this Coghlan's version looks to be the same handle that comes in the Opinel Garden Knife #8. It is the curved design with the size and heft of the standard Opinel. This Coghlan's version is perfect size and model for me. This knife comes in three sizes, "7, #8, and #9. The #8 fits my hand perfectly.

The carbon blade requires special care. To avoid tarnishing and rusting keep a very thin coat of oil on the blade and avoid acid such as are found in fruits. If you want this knife in stainless steel with a drop point blade shape rather than the standard clip point check out the Opinel Garden Knife #8.
text_fidelity_b: Coghlans 0008 Camp Knife

VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight Good basic inexpensive sunglasses that block uv400 and are polarized. However, there are reviews on here saying these are a “high quality product.” These are good quality for the price point. But for this price obviously the frame is plastic, lenses are basic triacetate & can scratch easily, polarization film is on the outside of the lens which can degrade and are not very impact resistant.
Compare that to higher quality sunglasses (typically above $100) the lens material is likely to be polycarbonate. The polarized film is sandwiched between two layers of polycarbonate meaning the polarized film can never wear out and provides impact protection. That’s the big difference.
I like these glasses for just a basic pair to use for activities where I’m afraid to use my nicer sunglasses. Are these worth the price? Yes I believe these are a good value, have great looks and provide the basics. However, there are others out there for half this price that can provide the same basics but sometimes lack in style and fit.
I would say the glasses are a bit narrow on my face but I like the look and was surprised these were nicer than expected.
text_fidelity_b: VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight

text_fidelity_a:
Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer Download the manual from the Burley website.

This is our second Travoy trailer. The other is still in use after 10 years. The new Travoy has some substantial upgrades:

• The new “kickstand” design keeps the trailer upright when parked with a load. The old one would tip over.
• New seatpost hitch allows a single hitch to be shared among two or more bikes. With the old one you had to buy more hitches.
• The tow arm now extends to accommodate rear bike racks and larger MTB wheels.
• Tow arm is now padded with foam for hand comfort.

The entire time we owned our first Travoy we mistakenly believed we should have chosen a flatbed instead. We recently bought a flatbed and don’t use it; bought a second Travoy as a backup. If all you do is local errands the Travoy is by far the easiest and best. If you tour or travel dirt roads a flatbed might be a better choice but you should want both a flatbed plus the Travoy because the Travoy is easier for local errands which are far more common.

The bags that are dedicated for use with the Travoy are costly and do not hold enough. Instead, wheel your Travoy into Target or Walmart and choose the largest clothes hamper that fits the Travoy form factor (see photo). Attach that hamper with three ratcheting tie-downs or four high quality, ADJUSTABLE bungees. Do not skimp on quality or number.

PROS:
• Lightweight, 10lbs +/-
• No tools or setup required. Screw the hitch onto your seatpost with the T-bold and you’re done.
• Folds to easily fit in a backseat, a trunk or an airline overhead.
• Holds up to $125 in groceries with the large hamper attached. Mind the maximum weight restriction (60lbs) and pack the heaviest items at the bottom (66% of load) and lighter items at the top (33%).
• With the Travoy you don’t have to bend over quite as far to reach cargo.
• Comes with a storage/carrying bag (although it’s mostly useless for carrying cargo).

CONS:
• You must adjust your riding style slightly. The Travoy is stable on level pavement but may tip over at significant road imperfections or surface debris. Slow down and approach handicapped ramps and driveways exactly at 90 degrees (perpendicular) to avoid catching a wheel on their raised shoulders. Avoid potholes and debris entirely. You’ll grow accustomed to this over time and it will not bother you. If the Travoy DOES tip, it doesn’t take the bike with it.
• If you run with the stock tires and tubes be prepared for flats. The availability of high quality 12.5” inch tires and tubes is extremely limited. All the tires from Asia that we tried are no good, even dangerous. We found very high quality 12.5 inch tires from the German manufacturer “Schwalbe” (available here on Amazon). Schwalbe currently offers the “Road Cruiser” for street and the “Black Jack” for trails and off-road (12/2020).
• 12.5” thorn resistant tubes are available here on Amazon but the Travoy 12.5 inch wheels require a 45 degree valve; otherwise there is not enough room to attach a pump or even a pump hose. These thorn resistant tubes had straight valves. To accommodate this shortcoming we found a "Air Inflator Hose Adapter" here on Amazon. Although it just barely fits, we can use it with both our floor pump and our road pump.

TIPS:
• In addition to thorn resistant tubes, we use the “Mr. Tuffy”-brand tire inserts on all our bike and trailer wheels (here on Amazon). Flats are now a very rare occurrence and we ride among numerous desert thorns.
• When using the hamper it is easy to cut a neon yellow reflective vest into three sections (left front, right front and back) and attach the sections to the hamper (left side, right side and rear, see photo).
• Reflective flags and flagpoles with mounts that fit your hamper are available here on Amazon. The flagpole we bought is high enough so that the flag can be seen above the level of a parked car (see photo). For added safety we now use this flag and pole on our bikes even without the trailer.
• When the hamper is inappropriate we use a cargo net. The cargo net is also handy if your hamper is overflowing.

Leave a comment if you have questions.
text_fidelity_b: Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer

Lately though I have noticed pain in my forearms and hands, probably from lifts like barbell bench press. I'm giving these a shot.

They're made from thin breathable material, and the wrapping portion is about 3 feet long. The 'tie' is another 1.5 feet. Having it be long and thin gives the flexibility desired - you want it firm wrap tighter, flexible, make it more loose. The tie itself isn't super secure unless you spend time ensuring it is. Others I have seen use velcro which is probably easier to manage, but it might not be as secure.

Down sides: There's a couple of frays in thethreading, no carrying bag, and no instructions in the box. All stuff that shouldn't matter much.

However, these seem like they'll add the support I need, and won't be cumbersome to take with me. I'm looking forward to my next heavy "push" day to give this a run for its money.

Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead I received this as a free review sample. I am not going to repeat the product specs on this page since the material and unfolded dimensions are provided by the manufacturer. I will give my take on this and reasons why I rated it so highly.

What I especially like is the compact size that it folds to. Out of the box it's only 12.5x4x1 inches, which will fit in a backpack or even in the glove box of most vehicles (especially if you fold it over lengthwise.)

There is a slight chemical odor as soon as you unbox it, so I recommend airing it out before refolding and storing it for actual use. It takes about an hour for the odor to dissipate.

Using it is as simple as placing your valuables inside, folding over the reinforced rib at the top (the mouth) of the bag two or three times, then doubling and using the closure snaps. You are NOT supposed to press the air out because that will provide buoyancy in the event that it falls into water. I am not sure how much weight it will take to achieve negative buoyancy, but partially filled with air it will support a good five pounds and still maintain a degree of positive buoyancy. The key point and why I rated this so highly is I tested it with a towel and a brick and it kept the towel completely dry.

If you camp, boat or spend time at the beach and want to safeguard wallets, phones and tablets, this bag will do the trick.
text_fidelity_b: Ivation 5-Gallon Portable Outdoor Shower - Lightweight & Portable - Includes Removable Hose w/On-Off Switchable Showerhead

Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game: 2 Folding Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, Aluminum Frame with MDF Board Cornhole is a fun game that brings back memories of “Toss-Across” for me. I never had heard of, or played, cornhole until it was introduced to me at a social gathering relatively recently. I have wanted my own set for taking to family functions and picnics with friends, and this set is well suited for these situations.

I will start with this: I received the tailgate version which is a little smaller than the regulation size set. The difference is that the boards are a foot shorter. That’s ok, but it does mean that my set is not suitable for true tournament play and instead is geared for casual competition. Both sized sets are available here; make sure you get the size you want. While it may be a little smaller, it has two distinct advantages. First, it is lighter so it is easier to carry. Second, because it is smaller it is more compact and can be stored (and transported) more easily too.

This set is made to be portable. Most sets I have seen have been made of plywood and have fixed legs. To move them is awkward and often unwieldy. This set instead has an aluminum frame and lightweight boards so the weight is substantially reduced. The legs fold under, allowing the set to lay flat. This makes it a lot easier to pack the set for travel and to store it away when not in use. An important detail – when the legs are down they lock in place with a metal bracket so the board will not collapse.

The set comes with 8 bean bags, 4 blue and 4 red. These are regulation size and are interchangeable with other sets.

So far my family is very pleased with this set. It is made very well, it is compact and portable, and because this set (in my case) is the tailgate version it is lighter and easier to store when not in use. This is an easy product to recommend.

SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag Waterproof Accessory for Paddle Boarding If the devil is in the details this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag is made with a range of details that make it an outstanding, well thought out bag, and should be perfect for our Kayaking and SUPing trips. We haven’t been out on the water yet this year, but cannot wait to get back out and without doubt, this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag will be going along for the ride! When I had the chance to grab this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag I decided to so we had a nice bag to carry those things we might need on the water and have a place to keep our phone, wallets, and keys safe. I am so glad I did - and my wife is thrilled. This bag was designed by someone who has time on the water and it shows.

The materials are top notch and the construction equally great. You can tell by looking at the bag the materials are good. But get your hands on it and you feel it. The thickness, the strength, the stitching - it all comes together and promises longevity. We always pay attention to zippers and in this case, not only is the handle-zipper strong and secure, but it settles in perfectly so as to keep water out. There are the details here - straps on the back top at each side so you can grab and hold on as you “try” to open and close the zipper. It literally warns you it is a hard pull and it is! That simply means water is going to be working hard to get in there. And the straps do help pull it across - though you’re still going to be grabbing the bag at some point to help. It is that tight! No problem if it means protecting your gear. They even included zipper lube so you can keep those zippers in top condition - something to keep in mind when you’re on fresh or salt water! Really impressive they thought of these things!

The strap for carrying it is also well done, with good materials, good stitching, and a comfortable padding on the shoulder. The straps for attaching to the SUP or Kayak are strong and well secured - they should last a good long time. Additionally, the rope on the top front allows you to secure things like towels, tighten it down, and keep them secure. An included wet bag for your phone gives added protection for that special need-to-have equipment.

Overall, this is a great, well designed bag that I think anyone who spends time on the water will appreciate. Well thought out, well constructed, and well executed, you are going to find any number of reasons to have it with - on the SUP or kayak, at the pool, beach, or wherever you spend time. We have not tested the waterproof aspect - again, haven’t been to the water yet, but while we appreciate the promise, we always still try to keep things dry. We would likely use other smaller dry bags inside - just to be safe - but appreciate the effort here. In the end, we are thrilled to have this SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag.
text_fidelity_b: SUP-Now Stand Up Paddle Board Deck Bag Waterproof Accessory for Paddle Boarding

W WSTOO Snorkel Mask with Latest Dry Top Breathing System,Fold 180 Degree Panoramic View Full Face Snorkel Mask Anti-Fog Anti-Leak with Camera Mount,Snorkeling Gear for Adults and Kids We are preparing for our trip to Costa Rica and wanted to try a full face snorkel and this one looked pretty good. And right out of the box and after just a couple strap changes I have to say that it is very comfortable on. I have been reading about them and I was a little concerned about CO2 build up and problems getting the mask off in an emergency but that does not seem to be any problem.

We did run a test of the mask in the city pool and it was surprisingly free of leaks. I did have problems with some leakage when I dove and it does seem to do better when simply cruising along the surface as the mask changes its fit when diving. Breathing turned out to be very comfortable and the flipping snorkel was great. We had some issues with fogging immediately (note it was in a car at 7 degree Fahrenheit and brought into a steamy indoor pool.) but that seemed to have cleared up well once the mask was warm.

Clarity was not the best. It was definitely ok for my purposes, but there is a little distortion, especially in the bend of the lense. It is still definitely workable but a little distorted. I would guess there is better glass out there, but this is a pretty low price point. It should meet our expectations for the trip, but probably will not exceed them.

-----

Reaction after the trip - There was a bit of struggling with leaks around the mask, especially along eyes and hairline. It did fog a little, and it was hard to dive without all of these things getting a little worse. But if I stayed on the surface and took the mask off occasionally to clear water and fog. It worked well enough. It was a little bulky to pack and if you are serious about your snorkeling (we did about 6 hours in six days.) you may want a better fitting mask.
text_fidelity_b: W WSTOO Snorkel Mask with Latest Dry Top Breathing System,Fold 180 Degree Panoramic View Full Face Snorkel Mask Anti-Fog Anti-Leak with Camera Mount,Snorkeling Gear for Adults and Kids

Kids have been jumping on it with all the neighborhood kids. A little less bouncy than our 14 year old trampoline but once the springs get broken in should be a great bounce.
Pros- Huge, looks very safe, less pricey than other good quality trampolines, includes what is needed, each piece is heavy and heavy duty. Can hold hundreds of pounds.
Cons- The Premium netting takes 2 persons to put up because of the upper ring. Because of the upper netting frame, looks like it will very timely and hard to take down for snowy winters.

text_fidelity_a:
SmooSat SA3(Prime) Electric Scooter for Adults, 20/28 Miles Long Range, 350W Brushless Motor, 8.5/10” Solid Tire, 15.6/20 MPH Max Speed, App Control &Type-C Reverse Charging(Prime Only), LED-Display So my wife loves roller blading and after trying it a number of years back, we discover it is NOT my cup of tea. I miss out when she goes and was trying to think of ways I might still be able to go. I started seeing these eScooters and thought... why not? Had the chance to get one a couple of weeks ago and grabbed it. A short time later I would have the chance to get a second and grabbed it as well, allowing us both to use them when she's not blading.

We like both. Each has a couple "cons," but nothing we can't get over or around. And in the end, we really like them - both. They are each great fun to ride, easy to learn, and have let us enjoy some fun evening rides. Here's our take:

1. Our arrived in the very large box, folded, and needing some assembly before use.

2. There was sadly some damage to the box upon arrival, but didn't notice until - as we worked on the data box - that something seems to have poked a hole through the box, the interior stuffing, the instructions, and finally the end of the handlebars, leaving a gash in the material. It's disappointing, though we do not think caused any damage to how works. We worry about it getting wet in there - as parts to control the bike lie within - but we'll be careful. Though again, disappointing. It's not "brand new perfect."

3. The assembly was mostly easy. Pull up the handle into place, you do have to tighten/loosen/adjust with the included wrench that was truly not worth the cost of making it. One twice and it was slightly bent - but enough it wouldn't grip anymore. Had to use our own adjustable wrench. Got that worked out. Took a few adjustments, but it allows you to lock down the stick holding the handle bars. Once secure the stick and handles bars are very secure throughout the ride. The other eScooter we have allows the handlebars to drop down to fold in and carry in a bag - this does not - and while a nice feature, those also jiggle in a way that makes my wife unfordable while riding. I don't have a problem, but it is a consideration. So this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults makes for a smoother ride for my wife in that regard.

4. Once the stick and handlebars are locked into place, you're pretty much ready to go. It does go down, so you can store it folded, into a smaller piece. The rest of the footprint remains the same - meaning you only loose the height. We have left both open since assembly and find it is easy to get it in and out, but appreciate this feature. The one thing the other eScooter does is to fold down into a smaller overall package - though again, the same footprint size - and fits into an included carrying bag. This SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not do that. It is one feature that puts a point into the box for us with the other eScooter and not with this one. If you're working, going to school on a college campus, or maybe out for a ride and want to go in somewhere, being able to pack it into a bag and carry it is a nice feature this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not offer - though you can break it down and carry it by hand.

5. The SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults is also noticeably heavier than the other eScooter we got, but for each of us, not so much so we couldn't carry it a distance. You would notice the weight more quickly on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but to/from a house, car, or the like it's easy enough.

6. The deck here is pretty decent - size, shape, and traction. My wife feels comfortable on it, but has said a little more room would be nice. But these are eScooters and designed for being useful, but not big. Ironically I'm a bit bigger than her and I am fine - though note the size on both - but ride the smaller other one. Because...

7. With a bit of added weight, I currently do not fit within the posted weight limit of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - which is decidedly lower than the other eScooter. Therefore, for safety, I have not even tried this one yet. My wife rides it and does love it. However, the weight difference is interesting in that this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults IS larger and a bit heavier, but the other one comfortably takes my weight in it's posted limits. So it's a bit weird. We feel like this one would likely be fine as well, but won't try. But it also puts another check in the box for the other one.

8. Great bell. Decent light. We both feel like the bell - which sounds similar to a bike bell - is far better on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but the light are better on that one. This is doable, but not as large or as bright.

9. There are included tools for assembly, but again, the wrench was worthless after one turn, the others fine. We tossed the wrench, but kept the others if we need to adjust anything.

10. The range on this and the speed are great. I can't tell you off the top of my head what either are listed as, but we've been out and about over a few nights and gone a bit further each time. We're GenX and desk jockeys, so our activity levels had taken a dive - injuries and flu knocked us off our higher actives over the last year or so, though ironically not due to Covid. But getting on these has been a bit of a pacing task. We have been having to adjust to the standing in such a small spot and not moving - no room - so our feet are a bit... they are adjusting. It's been working and each ride we have been more and more comfortable - to the point we no longer stop for our feet being sore. Anyways, the point being, we are both still on the original charge, and we have gone some good distance as we learn and have fun. So we have not charged it yet to know how long. But we are very impressed with the distances we have so far gotten.

11. The speeds are excellent. Again, I've been riding the other one, but my wife easily keeps up. On that one I noticed my current weight does not limit my speed. That one has three speed levels and I'm in the middle. I THINK this one does as well and that she too is using the middle option. Her weight - well within the range of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - is no obstacle for her or this eScooter - she can go fast and feel it. We have done some decent "hill" climbing and decent and there is no struggle.

12. The Breaks - WORK! You STOP and you STOP! I mean, hit the breaks and she says it STOPS! The other one has a more reducing speed element - you push the button and it slows you, then you STOP with your feet. In her use of both eScooters, she actually prefers mine - the slowing rather than the STOP. She feels it's far TOO strong and she has to be careful of this so as not to knock herself off. It's not bad - not like she won't use it or is scared of using it - but the reducing speed almost feels like it gives her more control. We have not - yet and hopefully never - had a need to just STOP, but if we did, she's golden.

13. But the reducing speed on the other one allows me to go into controlled corners without stopping, but rather controlling the eScooter. I have a far wider range of speed levels it gives me to do intricate and controlled movements, rather than having to let it "naturally" slow down and do the same on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults. So two different experiences of control in this way.

In the end, this is a REALLY FUN and well built eScooter. My wife loves it and I look forward to being able to try it when the weight is back down. In the mean time, we can both get out there, go for rides, and have fun. We are thrilled to have it. But... if we had to pick a single eScooter type/make to have, we both agree, we'd likely pick the other one. There is nothing they could have done - again, we feel it was a delivery issue - about the damage to the handlebar. It's disappointing, but we do not hold the eScooter or company responsible.

So that leaves the idea the other one can be broken down and carried in a bag, this one only broken down. This one IS a bit heavier. This one is a bit more of a process to put the handlebars up and down. This one does not have the same weight restrictions as the other - by a long shot of at least 30 lbs difference - meaning larger folks are more limited - check before you buy how much it can hold - so this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults one right away eliminated me from using it until I get these pounds back off. And the STOPPING of this being so abrupt is not our preference.

But in the end, we still truly love this eScooter. It IS a great ride and we have had fun being out. My wife is enjoying it very much. Would we pick the other if we had to? Yes. But for an eScooter, this one is really nice. We cannot - at present - give it anything less than 5 stars for what it does do - meaning we wouldn't drop any stars because of what it doesn't. We're happy to have this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults.
text_fidelity_b: SmooSat SA3(Prime) Electric Scooter for Adults, 20/28 Miles Long Range, 350W Brushless Motor, 8.5/10” Solid Tire, 15.6/20 MPH Max Speed, App Control &Type-C Reverse Charging(Prime Only), LED-Display

What does that mean? Well, if you are visiting or living in a country where tap isn't safe to drink, using this bottle will not change that.

HOWEVER, if your tap is safe to drink but you don't like the taste and the chlorine, this is a great option. The filter supposedly lasts through 300 uses, which makes this bottle, valued at $9.99 at the time of the review, worth the minor expense. You save money and reduce your environmental impact.
Nice bottle!
